statement: When the chain moves an Account's epoch on, the Entity restarts the Account from what the chain holds. The new epoch counts offdelta from zero in every token (R-IMPLICIT-BASELINE), so every ledger takes offdelta 0, in the committed state and in the state a pending frame of the node would commit (the same two states R-J-COLLATERAL keeps in line with the chain), and the node forgets the peer's signature over a head of the voided epoch (a dispute from it would only revert: the ask is refused for want of a proof, `no_proof`). The epoch moves in three places in Account.sol (`_advanceOndeltaEpoch`): a dispute finalize pays the Account out (the proof's offdelta is paid in cash, collateral and ondelta reset), a C2R (signed only at offdelta zero, R-C2R-FOLD) and a settlement (the node signs every fold, so the offdelta lands in ondelta through the AccountSettled snapshot). `j_dispute_over` is the dispute finalized (a counter is `j_countered`, not its end): it also sets collateral and ondelta to zero for every token the Account has a ledger for and every token the Entity kept a row for, since the chain emits no AccountSettled for it. This is wider than the contract: the finalize pays and resets only the tokens of the proof body (Depository.sol 921-927), so a token the chain holds with no ledger, or whose ledger came after the proof, keeps its collateral on chain while both Entities say zero (Review A H1 on #159). Both sides understate alike, so frames agree and no money moves wrongly; capacity and withdrawals for that token are refused too early until the next AccountSettled for it. Owed: zero only the proof's tokens, or read the holdings at the end of the finalizing block. Assumption (Review A H2): a finalized `j_dispute_over` carries no epoch, so it is delivered once and in order (R-HEIGHT-ORDER); one delivered after a later `j_collateral` would zero that deposit. A repeat or older report of the epoch changes nothing. A frame in flight is kept: if the peer committed it before it heard of the move it re-acks it whatever its epoch and both sides hold the same rebased ledger; if it refuses it as another epoch's, the node's view has moved, so it takes the frame back and proposes its txs again under the new epoch on the rebased state, where one that no longer fits is refused back to whoever asked. The signature a frame's ack brings is kept as the peer's proof only when the frame was sealed in the epoch the node signs in now: an ack that commits a frame across the epoch move keeps the head and drops the signature. A payment the peer committed after the proof a dispute started from is voided with that dispute unless the peer counters it with the newer proof (R-DISPUTE-WATCH: the counter lands, e2e step dispute-stale), so this e2e step loses the payment on the link before the peer commits it. A frame the node would commit in the gap between the chain's finalize and its own Entity hearing of the epoch move is refused: the Account is quiet until the finalize is heard (R-DISPUTE-FREEZE); a frame sealed before the dispute was heard and acked after it is the one left, and with no counter the finalize voids it: each side is told the offdelta it counted when the epoch moves (`offdelta_rebased`, R-DISPUTE-FREEZE), not what the chain paid (owed: a notice for offdelta beyond the finalized proof, whose body hash the DisputeFinalized event carries). Owed: open holds at the move (S9: the clause resolves on the chain and the ledger's holds are not dissolved here), the Depository's debts a finalize creates, and the signed-unsuperseded list of the old epoch still counts against the cap of 64.
source: coordinator 10-02 (S10 rebase, design accepted 10:24); plan/s10-rebase-design.md; Account.sol 921, 1385, 1743

layers.arrival: n/a: the Arrival page models the Account's frames within an epoch; what the Entity does when the chain moves the epoch is an Entity rule, and the spec thread owes the epoch move as a step of its model
layers.quint: n/a: the Quint model has the chain's cells; the Entity's ledger after an epoch move is not one of them
layers.contract: n/a: the contract moves the epoch and resets what it holds; this row is what the Entity does with it, and the e2e rebase step reads both sides against the chain

killers.name: R-LEDGER-REBASE every token's offdelta is zero and everything else of the Account is as it was
R-LEDGER-REBASE rebasing twice changes nothing, and an Account with no ledger has none to rebase
R-LEDGER-REBASE every offdelta is zero again, limits stay, and the proof of the old epoch is forgotten
R-LEDGER-REBASE a repeat or an older report of the epoch changes nothing, a new payment stays
R-LEDGER-REBASE a Host that restarts after the move replays to the same rebased Account
R-LEDGER-REBASE a frame the peer committed before the move commits on both, with one ledger
R-LEDGER-REBASE the re-ack of an old epoch's frame leaves neither side a proof of that epoch
R-LEDGER-REBASE a frame the peer never heard is refused as another epoch's and sealed again
R-LEDGER-REBASE a payment that fitted only before the move is refused back to the one who asked
R-LEDGER-REBASE after a finalize collateral, ondelta and offdelta are zero for every token
R-LEDGER-REBASE a dispute that is over by a counter keeps what the chain holds
R-LEDGER-REBASE a token with no ledger that the chain held something for is zeroed too
